the integration of CNT arrays with thick-film TE material by electrodeposition.
the integration of thick-film TE elements with CNTs for TE devices.
the design of a scalable process to integrate TE elements with compliant CNT arrays, and the characterization of the thermal and thermomechanical properties of the integrated TE/CNT structures.

the CNT arrays are a viable and scalable platform for the integration of thick-film TE elements.

the results of this study demonstrate that CNT arrays provide an excellent interface between TE films and metallic interconnects, and that CNT arrays also provide a means to enhance the fatigue life of TE devices.

the results of the present work show that the proposed electrodeposition method is capable of producing high quality TE materials with CNT arrays, and the resulting films have excellent thermomechanical and thermal contact characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CNT array electrodeposition process is effective for producing thick films of Bi2Te3 on CNT arrays.
the electrodeposited Bi2Te3 film on the CNT arrays was mechanically stable, and exhibited comparable electrical and thermal properties as compared to films electrodeposited on bare substrates.
CNT arrays can provide an excellent platform for heterogeneous integration of TE materials with metallic interconnects and substrates for the design of TE devices.

electrodeposition of thick Bi2Te3films on CNT arrays is a scalable process that can be used to fabricate compliant TE devices for cooling applications at room temperature.
